posts.author: Solar_Flare
posts.body:
Gensun said:
However, no algorithm, except generative AI, will increase the resolution of these assets. People pointing at a blurry picture and saying "enhance" to unblur a picture? That's hollywood. That doesn't exist IRL.
Click to expand...
I feel like there's a bit of a misunderstanding here?
If the goal is to obtain the "original pre-blurred image", then yeah, there's nothing. That means you're trying to recover details that were blurred out of existence, but those details are gone, so there's nothing to work with. I doubt even generative AI can reliably reconstruct them – at best it can produce an educated guess as to what the original image was like. It may even be a really good educated guess, but it's unlikely to be identical to the original.
But if you just want the image to be less blurry and don't care about the little details, then tools like "sharpen" or "increase contrast" can totally help.

posts.author: ELandP
posts.body:
These are amazing, if you want to scale these up for RPG Maker MZ's 48 x 48 tileset, then you'll need to use Nearest Neighbor sampling for the upscale. But MZ supports different size tilesets now.
I'm curious where I can find more RPG Maker 2003 RTP stuff ported to RPG Maker MZ, I heard someone did it in full on here but I can't seem to find it.

posts.author: Solar_Flare
posts.body:
ELandP said:
then you'll need to use Nearest Neighbor sampling for the upscale.
Click to expand...
I wouldn't recommend this – it'll make it hopelessly blurry. It might be okay for the water but probably not for things like trees.
If you're using GIMP, the best you can manage is probably "no interpolation". Beyond GIMP, xBRZ is quite successful as long as you're scaling by an integer multiple, and RM2k uses 16x16 tiles (exactly one-third of MZ's 48x48), so it might work here.

posts.author: Solar_Flare
posts.body:
Using None for interpolation will mean that every pixel becomes 9 pixels in the resulting image, making it look pixellated. That's fine if it fits your aesthetic though. However, if you want to avoid a pixellated look, xBRZ is a much better choice than Nearest Neighbour (unfortunately GIMP doesn't support it as far as I know).
Incidentally, I think RPGMaker 2003 actually upscales the 16x16 tiles to 32x32 automatically, using no interpolation. So, you're sort of getting a 1.5 increase for free because of that.
